Ahmedabad.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Ahmedabad.method: Capital Value: Area x Base Rate x Location Factor (F1, jantri-based)
Ahmedabad.formula: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) taxes vacant residential land under the Capital Value method: General Tax = Area (sq.m) × Base Rate (₹/sqm/yr) × F1 (location factor). For a standalone vacant plot the age, usage/structure, and occupancy factors all collapse to 1.0, so the formula reduces to Area × Base Rate × F1. F1 is set by the jantri (circle rate) band of the specific plot — Posh (F1=1.60), Good (1.10), Medium (0.90), Poor (0.60) — rather than by neighbourhood name, though four representative zones (Satellite/Bodakdev/Vastrapur/Prahlad Nagar as Posh; Naranpura/Paldi/Vasna as Good; Naroda/Amraiwadi as Medium; outer AMC limits as Poor) were used to anchor the database.

Ajmer.method: Urban Development Tax: (Area sq.yd x DLC Rate) / 2000
Ajmer.formula: Ajmer levies Urban Development (UD) Tax under Rajasthan's UD Tax Rules: UD Tax = (Plot Area in sq.yd × DLC Residential Rate in ₹/sq.yd) ÷ 2000. The tax is construction-neutral — a wholly vacant plot is taxed identically to a built one of the same area, since the formula runs on plot area regardless of construction (a genuine contrast with Madhya Pradesh, which penalises unbuilt plots after three years). Plots of or under 300 sq.yd are exempt; because the project's standard 1,200 sqft (133.33 sq.yd) plot falls under this threshold and would return ₹0, Ajmer uses 350 sq.yd, matching the Rajasthan-wide exception already applied elsewhere in this database.

Ambala.formula: Ambala City (Municipal Corporation Ambala City, distinct from the separately-administered Ambala Cantonment) taxes vacant land above 250 sq.yd via a collector-rate-linked formula under the Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1994: Tax = Collector Rate (₹/sqyd) × 0.00015 × Plot Area (sqyd). The project uses a 350 sq.yd plot to clear the 250 sq.yd threshold and enter the collector-rate-based (rather than flat-rate) bracket, capturing the genuine spatial gradient across Tehsil Ambala City's 16 collector-rate zones.

Amritsar.method: ARV: 5% of (Collector Rate x Area), taxed at 0.20%
Amritsar.formula: Amritsar Municipal Corporation (a Category 'A' municipality, grouped with Jalandhar, Ludhiana, Patiala, and SAS Nagar) computes vacant land tax via a three-step chain confirmed directly from its official self-assessment form: Total Plot Value = Area (sq.yd) × Collector Rate; Annual Rateable Value (ARV) = 5% of Total Plot Value; Vacant Land Tax = ARV × 0.20%. Combined, this reduces to Collector Rate × Area × 0.0001. The formula was cross-checked against the Municipal Corporation Amritsar (MCA) portal's official worked example, which reproduces the identical arithmetic template used by the Ludhiana (MCL) portal — confirming both cities apply the same statewide Punjab formula.

Bangalore.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Bangalore.method: Unit Area Value (UAV) self-assessment: GAV x 20% tax + 24% cess
Bangalore.formula: Bangalore (BBMP) uses the Unit Area Value (UAV) self-assessment system. For vacant land: Gross Annual Value (GAV) = Area (sqft) × UAV (₹/sqft/month) × 10 months (BBMP allows a 2-month vacancy deduction); Property Tax = 20% of GAV; Cess = 24% of Property Tax (combined Health, Library, and Beggary Cess); Total Tax = Property Tax + Cess, which always works out to 24.8% of GAV. UAV rates are set by Zone (A through F) and Category (XV under the 2008 notification, renumbered XIII under 2016).

Bareilly.method: Confirmed VLT = ₹0 (vacant land exempt per Nagar Nigam)
Bareilly.formula: UNRESOLVED. Bareilly's workbook contains circle rates (₹/sqm land value) for four localities, sourced from IGRS UP valuation lists at Sub-Registrar Sadar, Bareilly — but no confirmed annual vacant-land tax figure. The UP Municipal Corporation (Property Taxes) Rules, 2000 confirms that Annual Value for vacant land is derived from the circle rate ('having regard to' the Stamp Act circle rate) but does not specify a public, confirmed conversion factor from circle rate to rent rate, nor a confirmed tax percentage specifically applicable to vacant land in Bareilly.

Begusarai.method: Flat road-tier rate (Bihar Rule 9): Rs. 5/4/3 per sq.m by road class
Begusarai.formula: Begusarai Nagar Nigam applies Bihar's statewide flat road-tier VLT rate under Rule 9 of the Bihar Property Tax (Assessment, Collection and Recovery) Rules, 2013: Municipal Corporation tier — Principal Main Road ₹5/sqm/yr, Main Road ₹4/sqm/yr, Others ₹3/sqm/yr. This formula was independently verified to the rupee against Gaya's live tax calculator elsewhere in this project, and Begusarai is confirmed a Municipal Corporation (matching the applicable rate row) via its MVR portal Circle Name and Wikipedia infobox.

Bharatpur.method: Urban Development Tax: (Area sq.yd x DLC Rate) / 2000
Bharatpur.formula: Bharatpur applies the same Rajasthan UD Tax formula as Ajmer: Tax = (Plot Area in sqyd × DLC Interior Rate in ₹/sqyd) ÷ 2000, with residential plots up to 300 sqyd exempt. The project's 350 sqyd standard plot clears this threshold. Six localities were used — more than the usual four — to capture a richer gradient.

Chennai.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Chennai.method: Basic Street Rate (BSR) x Area x 12, taxed at 12.4% (post-2022)
Chennai.formula: Chennai (Greater Chennai Corporation) is documented across three distinct historical eras, each with its own formula. Era 1 (2001–2008): a fixed flat rate of ₹8/month per 2,400 sqft (one Ground), independent of location, with tax computed via a four-grade slab (Grade I–IV) applied to Annual Value. Era 2 (2009–March 2022): Basic Street Rate (BSR) × Area × 12 = Annual Value, taxed via the same slab structure. Era 3 (April 2022 onward): Revised BSR × Area × 12 = Annual Value, taxed at a flat 12.4% (9.0% General Tax + 2.5% Education Tax + 0.9% Library Cess).

Coimbatore.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Coimbatore.method: Flat location value (Rs./sqft) x Area + 10% Library Cess
Coimbatore.formula: Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation (CCMC) levies Vacant Land Tax as a distinct, named tax under the Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Rules 2023: a flat location value in ₹ per sqft applied directly to plot area, with no circle-rate multiplier and no ARV conversion step. Basic VLT = Area × Location Value; General Tax = Basic VLT; Library Cess = 10% of General Tax; the two summed give the half-yearly VLT, doubled for the annual figure.

Dehradun.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Dehradun.method: Monthly Rate (vacant-plot category) x Area x 12, taxed at 12.5%
Dehradun.formula: Dehradun Nagar Nigam assesses vacant land under a four-category system (A: RCC/pucca building; B: other pucca; C: kuchcha; D: residential plot with no building, i.e. vacant land), each with three road-width bands (<12m, 12-24m, >24m). Annual Value = Plot Area (sqft) × Monthly Rate (₹/sqft/month, Category D, road-width band) × 12; Property Tax = AV × 12.5%. The <12m road-width band is used throughout as representative of a typical residential holding.

Delhi.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Delhi.method: Unit Area Method: Area x UAV x Vacant Factor (0.5) x Tax Rate (7-12%)
Delhi.formula: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) computes vacant land tax via the Unit Area Method: Annual Value = Land Area (sqm) × Use Factor (1.0) × Unit Area Value (colony-category-specific, ₹/sqm) × Occupancy Factor (1.0) × Vacant Land Fixed Factor (0.5); Annual VLT = Annual Value × Tax Rate (12% for Category A/B, 11% for C-E, 7% for F-H, residential). Delhi's eight colony categories (A highest-value to H, rural villages) each carry a distinct Unit Area Value.

Dewas.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Dewas.method: ALV = Factor (Rs./sqft) x Area; PT (3-6%) + flat + Urban + Edu Tax
Dewas.formula: Dewas Municipal Corporation applies Madhya Pradesh's ALV-based flat-factor system to vacant plots (Sampatti Kar): Annual Letting Value = Factor (₹/sqft/yr, zone-specific) × Plot Area (sqft); Annual Tax = Property Tax (3% of ALV through 2022-23, 6% from 2023-24) + Samekit Kar (a flat ₹300 or ₹500 depending on zone) + Urban Tax (1% of ALV, Zone 1/2 only) + Education Tax (2% of ALV). Four zone-stable localities were used: Civil Lines (Zone 1), Colony Nai Abadi (Zone 2), Kalukhedi (Zone 3), Indra Nagar Jhuggi Jhopdi (Zone 4).

Gaya.method: Flat road-tier rate (Bihar Rule 9): Rs. 5/4/3 per sq.m by road class
Gaya.formula: Gaya Ji Municipal Corporation applies Bihar's flat, road-tier-based VLT: Annual VLT = Road-Tier Rate (₹/sqm) × Area (sqm), where the rate is fixed by Rule 9 of the Bihar Property Tax (Assessment, Collection and Recovery) Rules, 2013 at ₹5/sqm for Principal Main Road, ₹4/sqm for Main Road, and ₹3/sqm for Others — a flat statutory scale, not a percentage of market or capital value, which sets Bihar apart from every other state in this database.

Gwalior.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Gwalior.method: ALV = Area x Zone Factor; Property Tax = 6% of ALV (Rule 8)
Gwalior.formula: Gwalior Municipal Corporation treats Open Land as a distinct construction type under the MP Municipal Corporation Act 1956 and the MP Municipality (Determination of Taxable Property Value of Building/Land) Rules 2020: Annual Letting Value = Area (sqft) times Rate Zone Factor (rupees per sqft per year, zone-specific); Total Property Value = ALV (no divergence found across 17 years of records); Property Tax = 6.00% of TPV exactly, in every taxed observation — the Rule 8 statutory band is 6-10%, and Gwalior sits at the floor. Urban Tax (1%) and Education Tax (1%) of TPV are added, plus a flat, zone-independent Sameketik Kar charge that grew from ₹240 to ₹500 over the study period and is levied even on exempt plots.

Hisar.formula: Hisar (Municipal Corporation Hisar) uses the same collector-rate-linked formula as Ambala under the Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1994: Tax = Collector Rate (rupees per sqyd) times 0.00015 times Plot Area (sqyd) for plots above 250 sqyd, with a 350 sqyd standard plot used to enter this bracket and capture the spatial gradient across four localities (Sector 13 core-posh, Sector 9-11 core-mid, Satrod Kalan semi-peripheral, Ludas periphery village).

Hyderabad.method: Capital Value: 0.5% of (Area x Circle Rate)
Hyderabad.formula: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) levies Vacant Land Tax as 0.5% of the Capital Value of land, where Capital Value = Area (sq.yd) times Government Circle Rate (rupees per sq.yd) sourced from the IGRS Telangana registration-value system. Four tiers were used based on confirmed IGRS rates rather than discrete named zones: Tier 1 Prime (Jubilee Hills Road 1), Tier 2 Secondary (Banjara Hills Road 4-9), Tier 3 Mid-city (Amberpet), Tier 4 Outer (Sai Nagar).

Indore.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Indore.method: ALV = Area x Zone Land Rate; Tax = ALV x Zone Rate (1-6%) + 8% cess
Indore.formula: Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC) uses an Annual Letting Value method with five confirmed rate zones under the MP Municipality (Determination of Annual Letting Value of Building/Lands) Rules, 1997: ALV = Area (sqft) times Land Rate (Zone-specific, confirmed at ₹18/15/12/9/6 per sqft per year for Zones 1-5); Property Tax = ALV times Tax Rate% (a confirmed 1-6% band, but the exact zone-by-zone percentage mapping is not published, so this database uses a linear interpolation across the confirmed band, explicitly flagged as an assumption); Library Cess = 8% of Property Tax.

Jaipur.method: Urban Development Tax: (Area sq.yd x DLC Rate) / 2000
Jaipur.formula: Jaipur Municipal Corporation (JMC) levies Urban Development Tax via the simplest formula in this database: UD Tax = (Plot Area in sq.yd times DLC Residential Rate in rupees per sq.yd) divided by 2000 — no multiplicative factors, no slab rates, no cess components. Uniquely among the Rajasthan cities in this project, Jaipur uses a 300 sq.yd standard plot — its own statutory minimum-taxable threshold — rather than the 350 sq.yd convention applied to Ajmer and Bharatpur, since JMC's exemption rule states plots 'of or under 300 sq.yd' are tax-free and 300 sq.yd is therefore the smallest plot size that yields a non-zero, genuinely comparable figure for this specific corporation.

Jalandhar.method: ARV: 5% of (Collector Rate x Area), taxed at 0.5%
Jalandhar.formula: Municipal Corporation Jalandhar (MCJ) applies the same post-2013 Punjab ARV formula family as Amritsar and Ludhiana, but without the Fire Cess shown on Ludhiana's worked examples: Plot Value = Collector Rate (rupees per sqyd) times Area; ARV = 5% times Plot Value; Property Tax = 0.5% times ARV — combined, Tax = 0.025% times Collector Rate times Area.

Kalaburagi.method: Capital Value System: % on Guidance Value (regime-dependent)
Kalaburagi.formula: Kalaburagi City Corporation's vacant-land tax was captured via the corporation's own online property tax calculator rather than a published rate table, entered directly by the researcher for four localities across three filing years. The stated formula moves from an Old Regime (2015-16 and 2020-21: 0.1% on 50% of Guidance Value) to a New Regime (2026-27: 0.2% on 25% of Guidance Value) — both of which reduce to the identical effective headline rate of 0.05% of Guidance Value.

Kolhapur.method: Capital Value: RR Rate x Area x 0.50 (vacant factor) x 0.25%
Kolhapur.formula: Kolhapur Municipal Corporation (KMC) applies Maharashtra's Capital Value System: Capital Value = Ready Reckoner Land Rate (rupees per sqm) times Plot Area (sqm) times 0.50 (vacant land factor); KMC Tax = Capital Value times 0.25%. Combined: VLT = RR Rate times 0.13935. Four localities span the confirmed core-to-periphery gradient, with two drawn from the same ward (Kasaba Karvir Ward D, Survey 4/112 and 4/106) to distinguish core-posh from core-mid tiers.

Kolkata.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Kolkata.method: Unit Area Assessment: BUAV x Area x Usage MF (2.0 for vacant) x tax%
Kolkata.formula: Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) is documented across three eras. Era 1 (pre-April 2017, Annual Rateable Value system): AV was 7% of market value for 2001/2006, or 2.5% of market value for plots up to 5 cottah for 2011/2016, taxed on a sliding scale from 11% to 40% depending on AV. Era 2 (April 2017-March 2025, Unit Area Assessment): Annual Value = Base Unit Area Value (BUAV, category-specific) times Area (sqft) times Location MF times Usage MF times Age MF times Structure MF times Occupancy MF, taxed at rates from 6% to 20% depending on category, plus a Howrah Bridge Tax surcharge in most wards. Era 3 (April 2025 onward): the same UAA formula, with a 10% hike applied to the property-tax component only.

Lucknow.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Lucknow.method: AV = Area x Monthly Land Rate x 12; General Tax = AV x 15%
Lucknow.formula: Lucknow Nagar Nigam (LNN) computes General Tax on vacant land under the UP Municipal Corporations Act, 1959 (Section 148): Annual Value = Plot Area × Monthly Land Rate (₹/sqft/month, ward-specific, varying by road width) × 12; General Tax = Annual Value × 15%. Land rates come from the ward-wise monthly rental rate schedule effective 1 April 2010. Four wards were selected to span the gradient: Ward 29 and Ward 57 (Zone 1, core), Ward 78 and Ward 97 (Zone 6, periphery), using the 12-24m road-width tier as the representative rate. This mechanism is worth distinguishing explicitly from the other two Uttar Pradesh cities in this database, since all three fall under the same parent UP Municipal Corporations Act, 1959 and Sampatti Kar Niyamavali framework yet arrive at genuinely different outcomes: Lucknow has a fully confirmed, single-percentage (15%) formula and a real ward-wise rate table, but that rate table itself has never been revised since 2010, so the entire city's spatial gradient is frozen at a fifteen-year-old snapshot; Varanasi also has a fully confirmed formula (the strongest-verified in this project, matched to an actual citizen tax bill down to the rupee) but uses a TWO-TIER percentage (10%/15% or 11%/15% depending on document vintage, rather than Lucknow's flat 15%) and a genuinely different rate table structure (Minimum Monthly Rent Rate rather than Lucknow's road-width-banded Land Rate); Bareilly, by contrast, has confirmed circle-rate (land value) data but NO confirmed tax percentage at all -- Bareilly Nagar Nigam's own website states vacant land is 'generally exempt,' and this project records a confirmed VLT of Rs0 for that city rather than apply either Lucknow's or Varanasi's percentage to it. All three cities therefore illustrate a single statutory family producing three distinct real-world outcomes: a frozen-but-real tax (Lucknow), a two-tier real tax independently verified against an actual bill (Varanasi), and a confirmed non-tax (Bareilly).

Ludhiana.method: ARV: 5% of (Collector Rate x Area), taxed at 0.5% + 10% Fire Cess
Ludhiana.formula: Municipal Corporation Ludhiana (MCL) computes vacant land tax for standalone plots in the 100-500 sq.yd bracket via: Plot Value = Collector Rate (₹/sqyd) × Area; ARV = 5% × Plot Value; Property Tax = 0.5% × ARV; Fire Cess = 10% × Property Tax; Total = Property Tax + Fire Cess = Property Tax × 1.10. The project's 1,200 sqft standard plot (133.33 sq.yd) was explicitly verified to fall within this bracket before the formula was applied.

Mangalore.method: Capital Value System: 25% of Guidance Value x Area x Rate%
Mangalore.formula: Mangaluru City Corporation (MCC) is documented across two regimes, built from real Self-Assessment Scheme (SAS) tax receipts rather than a projected standard-plot model. The Old Regime (confirmed frozen from at least 2008-09 through FY2022-23) is not derivable from a simple Guidance Value × Area × Rate formula — every tested receipt showed a 100-500× mismatch against that naive calculation — and is instead partially reconstructed as Tax(year) ≈ the plot's own 2008-09 base tax × a cumulative enhancement-window multiplier published by MCC itself. The New Regime (Capital Value System, confirmed operative from FY2023-24 onward) follows: Taxable Value/sqft = 25% × Guidance Value/sqft; Total Taxable Value = that figure × Area; Base Tax = Total Taxable Value × Rate% (0.2% confirmed for Residential); Final Tax = Base Tax × (1 + 3% Enhancement)^n.

Mumbai.method: Capital Value: SDRR x 0.25 (vacant weight) x FSI x Area x 1.63%
Mumbai.formula: Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC/MCGM) uses the Capital Value System, introduced in December 2012 with retrospective effect from 1 April 2010: Capital Value (open land) = Base Value (Ready Reckoner/SDRR rate) × User Category weightage × FSI × Land Area; Annual VLT = Capital Value × Tax Rate%. The database uses Item 18 ('Open land not built upon until issuance of I.O.D.', weightage 0.25) rather than Item 11 ('Open land - residential', weightage 1.00), confirmed via a live MCGM calculator printout as the correct category for land genuinely held vacant with no construction started. FSI is held at 1.0 throughout as a baseline assumption.

Nagpur.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Nagpur.method: Rent = UAV x Area x 12; ALV = Rent x 0.80; slab Gen./Water Tax + cesses
Nagpur.formula: Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) computes tax on vacant land (classified as 'open plots' under the same Residential usage weightage as a built house) via: Annual Rent = Area (sqm) × Unit Area Value (₹/sqm/month, Block-specific) × 12 × Usage Factor (1.0); Annual Letting Value = Annual Rent × 0.80 (a 20% statutory deduction); General Tax (slab, 14-30% of ALV) + Water Tax (slab, 10-15% of ALV) + flat components (18% combined: Sewerage, Water Benefit, Fire, Street, Municipal Education, Tree) + Government Education Tax (a state-level slab tax, 2-6% of ALV) = Full Total.

Nizamabad.method: Capital Value: 0.5% of (Area x Guideline Value)
Nizamabad.formula: Nizamabad Municipal Corporation applies the same Telangana capital-value formula confirmed for Hyderabad and Warangal: VLT (annual) = 0.5% × Capital Value, where Capital Value = Total Area (sq.yd) × Guideline Market Value (₹/sq.yd). This city's workbook is structured around two genuinely separate, non-overlapping datasets that could not be reconciled against each other despite deliberate attempts: Dataset A, three real VLTIN tax assessment records pulled directly from NMC's live payment portal; and Dataset B, thirteen representative localities from the Telangana Registration & Stamps Department's current guideline-value table, a rate benchmark not tied to any real assessed property.

Patna.formula: Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC) uses the simplest formula of any city in this database: Annual Property Tax = Vacant Land Area (sqft) × Vacant Land Road Factor — a direct final ₹/sqft/year rate with no separate Annual Value step and no percentage tax rate layered on top. The Municipal Corporation road factors are ₹0.46/sqft/year (Principal Main Road), ₹0.37 (Main Road), and ₹0.28 (Other Road). Three representative roads (rather than the usual four localities) were used, since Patna's factor has only these three fixed national values with no further locality-by-locality variation.

Ranchi.method: Flat road-width-tier rate (Rs./sq.m/yr, no ward gradient)
Ranchi.formula: Ranchi Municipal Corporation (RMC) levies Holding Tax on vacant land under the Jharkhand Municipal Act, 2011 (Section 152) as a flat per-sqm annual charge collapsing the ARV framework into a single levy: Tax = Area (sqm) × Rental Rate (₹/sqm/yr) × Occupancy Factor (1.0 for vacant land). The rental rate is set solely by road-width tier — 40ft+ (Principal Main Road), 20-39ft (Main Road), and under-20ft (Other Road) — with no ward-, zone-, or locality-specific gradient; Morabadi (Ward 3) and Namkum (Ward 13) confirmed to carry the identical rate at the same road width via a direct portal cross-check.

Rohtak.formula: Municipal Corporation Rohtak (MCR) levies Property Tax on vacant land under the Haryana Municipal Corporation Act, 1994 (Section 87(3) read with Section 149(1)), using the same collector-rate-linked formula confirmed for Ambala and Hisar under the identical statute and 2013 gazette notification: for a residential vacant plot above 250 sqyd, Tax = Collector Rate (Rs/sqyd) x 0.00015 x Plot Area (sqyd). As with Ambala and Hisar, a 350 sqyd plot is used rather than this project's standard 1,200 sqft (133 sqyd), since the smaller plot falls into a flat, no-gradient 101-250 sqyd exemption bracket that would not capture the collector-rate-based spatial variation this study needs.

Surat.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Surat.formula: Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) computes vacant-land property tax as Tax = MAX(R x F1 x F3 x Area(sqm), Minimum Tax), where R is the annual per-sqm base rate (Rs10/sqm confirmed 2010-11 through 2022-23, Rs12/sqm confirmed from 2023-24), F1 is a Market Location Factor set by Zone (A=1.50, B=1.30, C=1.10, D=0.90, E=0.70, F=0.50), and F3 is the 'Open Plot' Type-of-Property factor, confirmed at a fixed 0.10 for vacant land across every year checked -- a 90% discount relative to a fully-built Individual Bungalow (F3=1.00) on the same plot, the most explicit and severe vacant-land discount confirmed anywhere in this database. A Minimum Tax floor applies per tenement (Rs50/yr through 2022-23, Rs100/yr from 2023-24), overriding the formula result when the raw calculation falls below it.

Vadodara.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Vadodara.method: Property Tax: R (Rs./sqm) x Location x Open Plot Factor (0.50) x Area
Vadodara.formula: Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) computes property tax as R × M × A: ₹16/sqm from 2016 onward, treated as the confirmed rate through the current 2025 study year -- the ₹20/sqm figure sometimes cited for 2025 is a 2023 budget proposal never confirmed as formally adopted, and is not used in this database (see Data Constraints); M is the product of Location Factor (three confirmed classes, F1 = 1.25/1.00/0.75 for Class A/B/C), Age Factor, Usage Factor, and Occupancy Factor; A is the taxable area. For vacant land specifically, the Usage Factor uses a confirmed 'Open Plot' value of 0.50 — a moderate discount, roughly midway between Ahmedabad's absence of any dedicated vacant-land discount and the steeper 0.10 factor confirmed for Surat under the same Act family.

Varanasi.system: Zone or unit-area rate set by the city
Varanasi.method: AV = Area x Monthly Rent Rate x 12; Tax = AV x 10-15%
Varanasi.formula: Varanasi Nagar Nigam (VNN) computes vacant land tax via Annual Value (AV) = Plot Area (sqft) × Vacant-Land Minimum Monthly Rent Rate (₹/sqft, ward-wise, from an official VNN table) × 12; Tax = AV × 10% if AV is at or below ₹50,000, or × 15% above that threshold. This is the only city in the entire database with a fully sourced, zero-proxy formula that was independently cross-verified against a real citizen tax bill rather than relying on secondary-source description alone.

Vijayawada.method: Capital Value: 0.5% of (Area x Market Value, IGRS AP)
Vijayawada.formula: Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) applies Andhra Pradesh's standard capital-value formula: Annual VLT = 0.5% × Area (sq.yd) × Market Value (₹/sq.yd), with market values sourced from the AP Registration & Stamps Department's ward-wise sub-block valuation table. This workbook is restricted to Residential-classified sub-blocks only — an earlier version that included Commercial-classified rows was revised after Commercial rows were found to dominate two of the four originally-selected localities, collapsing their usable residential sample to as little as a single row.

Visakhapatnam.method: Capital Value: 0.5% of (Area x Guideline Value)
Visakhapatnam.formula: Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) applies the same 0.5%-of-capital-value formula confirmed for Hyderabad's GHMC: VLT = 0.5% × Guideline Value, where Guideline Value = Area (sq.yd) × IGRS AP Market/Guideline Rate. Four tiers were used: VIP Road (Tier 1, Core Prime), MVP Colony/Pedawaltair/Sector-1 (Tier 2, Core Secondary), Madhurawada Junction (Tier 3, growth corridor), and Sai Priya Layout (Tier 4, Periphery).

Warangal.method: Capital Value: 0.5% of (Area x Guideline Value)
Warangal.formula: Greater Warangal Municipal Corporation (GWMC) applies the same Telangana capital-value formula confirmed for Hyderabad and Nizamabad: Annual VLT = 0.5% × Capital Value, where Capital Value = Area (sq.yd) × Guideline Market Value. This workbook computes two figures per village rather than a single point: a Median value (the typical vacant plot in that village) and a Maximum value (the best-frontage main-road plot), letting within-village road-frontage premium be separated from cross-village geographic gradient.
